data.raw_text:
JUST IN: UP Manila College of Arts and Sciences Dean Ma. Theresa De Guzman has endorsed a Black Friday protest mobilization tomorrow, to be led by the College of Arts and Sciences Student Council (CASSC) and allied CAS organizations.

This comes after Rizal Hall’s sluggish renovation, which resulted in poor learning conditions and classroom shortage, was found to be tied to the controversial contractor companies owned by Sarah Discaya and Christopher Co. 

“Matagal nang nakatiwangwang ang renobasyon ng Rizal Hall ngunit hanggang ngayon ay patuloy na nagdurusa ang mga estudyante at guro sa masisikip at bulok na pasilidad,” CASSC’s statement reads.

42nd Student Regent Ron Dexter Clemente urged the student body in a Facebook post to join unit-wide walkouts, whether endorsed by their respective admins or not, to signify their unrest and disappointment with the multitude of infrastructure delays across UP campuses. 

Walkout mobilizations are also set to happen in UP Diliman, as endorsed by UP Diliman Chancellor Edgardo Vistan, UP Tacloban, and UP Diliman Extension Programs in Pampanga and Olanggapo (DEPPO).

#KurakotManagot

Left and right uprisings are sweeping the globe to prove one truth: ignored demands ignite revolt, and every act of defiance, even walkouts, is the people reclaiming what is theirs.

In rage against parliament’s bloated stipends, ten times the minimum wage, Indonesians storm politicians’ million-dollar mansions and torch their luxury. In France, petitions fail, barricades rise, and arrondissements burn under a rigid elite and brutal budget slashes. In Nepal, masses flood the streets, denouncing entrenched corruption and state-imposed censorship.

Our country is no exception. While floods drown entire communities, millions in taxpayer money vanish into the pockets of DPWH contractors through substandard projects. Responding to this decades-long deception, the people daub gates, deface facades timely calls, rally against the porcine displays of wealth bought from taxes.

The university is not sealed off from this reality. The Discaya-linked, stalled renovation of Rizal Hall exposes the same rot within our very own halls.

Students must rise with the masses, robbed and exploited. There is no wall between the campus and the peripheries writhing under injustice.

To walk out is to reject complicity, defend democracy, and confront a system that thrives on silence. Suppression only builds pressure; eventually, the Filipino voice erupts, and the cycle of betrayal shatters under its decision to resist.

Be one in resistance. Walkout.
UPM CAS Parking Lot | Sept. 12, 11:30 a.m.

READ: https://t.co/ufqLN6GEKw

𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐚: 𝐔𝐧𝐢𝐟𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝟗𝟏𝟏 𝐒𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐑𝐞𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐓𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭
MANILA — Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic  Remulla emphasized on Thursday that the official rollout of the Unified 911 System is a clear demonstration of the government’s commitment to good governance through responsive, timely, and efficient public service.
This in line with the call of President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. to restore public trust and ensure that every Filipino feels secure in their communities.
“We are the first responders. We are the last hope. This is governance,” Secretary Remulla stated, highlighting the critical role of emergency services in nation-building.
Speaking during the ceremonial launch, the DILG Chief hailed the Unified 911 System as a landmark initiative in public service delivery. “For the first time,  people will now have one number to call. People are assured of a response. People can rely on the government," he said.
The DILG affirmed that the Unified 911 System will be fully operational before the end of the year.
The centralized emergency hotline will cater to calls related to criminal activity, health emergencies, fire incidents, mental health concerns, and suspicious behavior. It will serve as a single point of contact, seamlessly integrating the response efforts of local government units (LGUs), the Philippine National Police (PNP), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), and the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP).
“This is the DILG’s long-standing aspiration — to establish a unified emergency response platform where the PNP, BFP, and BJMP work hand-in-hand to serve and protect the Filipino people,” Secretary Remulla added.
The BFP reiterated its commitment to a modernized, coordinated, and people-centered emergency response system — one that guarantees that help is always within reach. - DILG PRESS RELEASE

#RadyoPilipinas
